result.summary: This PR changes InitBlocksdirXorKey so that if blocks/xor.dat is missing but existing block files still start with the network magic (proving the data is XOR-obfuscated), the node throws an actionable error instead of silently writing a null key over the lost one. It adds a helper, BlocksdirDataIsObfuscated, that scans blk*.dat files for the magic bytes to distinguish a lost key from a fresh or pre-v28 unobfuscated blocksdir. Three new functional-test cases cover the lost-key, pre-v28-no-key, and single-damaged-file scenarios.
result.problem: When the xor.dat key file is lost, bitcoind currently stores a null key silently, then reports 'Corrupted block database detected' on the now-unreadable data. Following the node's suggested fix (-reindex) makes it worse: it completes without error, discards the chain down to height 0, and overwrites the block file start with a null-key genesis, so restoring the original key afterward still shows an empty chain on the first restart. This affects any user or operator whose xor.dat is separately lost (partial copy, storage fault) while block data is intact.
